summary: 40 units (81-120) on obstructed labour and surgical delivery. The draft is careful: no invented content, text flags plausible and kept out of src, damaged units handled with 'unclear'/conjectural marks. Main fixes: u107 Hindi attached the hand to the woman (error); Hindi jaṅghā vs jāँgh (sakthi), Hindi gloss/hedge gaps (basti, akṣikūṭa, maṇḍalāgra, aṅguliśastra, garbhaśayyā, apatyapatha, ākṣepa, jaghana), supplied '(it)' and 'लक्षण' (u86, u103, u109, u113), vāta vs vāyu (u115), conjectural mark for u88, striyam w. Open for owner: u86/u96 guess inside gloss, u104 īśvara, u106 udara disease vs belly, u108 chinnam eva, u113 śaṅku, u103 avadhārya vs avacārya. No regrouping needed (110-112, 115-116, 118-119 are one sentence each across units but should stay as printed).
glossary_suggestions: sakthi = जाँघ in Hindi (not जंघा, which the glossary uses for the lower leg) in the whole of ch04 u107-109.
avacārayet = 'should apply'; avacārya (if adopted in u103) = 'to be applied'.
śalya = 'dart' with 'foreign body' as second sense; use the same pair in all units (garbhaśalya u93 'the fetus as a dart').
mūḍhagarbha kept as technical term; modern equivalent 'obstructed labour / malpresentation (probable)' in notes at first use.
apatyapatha = 'path of the offspring (probably the birth passage)'; Hindi 'सन्तान का मार्ग यानी सम्भवतः प्रसव-मार्ग'.
jarāyu = 'afterbirth (jarāyu)' / जरायु यानी झिल्ली या जेर (strictly fetal membrane); aparā = 'placenta' / अपरा यानी जेर: keep the two apart in Hindi.
garbhaśayyā = 'bed of the fetus (probably the womb)'; garbhāśaya = womb (owner still has to settle womb vs uterus).
udara (u106 with aśmarī) = belly disease, probably ascites-type (probable); keep distinct from udara = belly (u85, u115).
Hindi vāta/वात only for the doṣa; plain wind (u115 vātapūrṇa, u118 vāyu) = वायु.
'(it)' is dropped when the object of an absolutive is not stated (u103, u109, u113); Hindi never takes the pronoun.
maṇḍalāgra and aṅguliśastra = instruments, 'probably a round-tipped knife' / 'probably a finger-knife', hedged in both languages; śaṅku = peg- or hook-like instrument (probable).
ākṣepa = convulsion (standard), Hindi आक्षेप यानी ऐंठन; makkala and saṃvaraṇa in u92 = unclear, mark in both translations.
A dṛti is a skin-bag/bellows; dṛteḥ iva ādhmātasya may be genitive: gram 'gen./abl.'
Use striyam (as printed) for the accusative of strī in w, not strīm, to avoid checker warnings.
